MINUTES
  MALIBU PLANNING COMMISSION
  SPECIAL MEETING
  MARCH l4. 2023
  TELECONFERENCED — VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  6:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to the Governor‘s Executive Orders N-25-20
and N-29—2O and fully teleconferenced fr0m various locations during the coronavirus
disease (COVID-l9) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Smith called the meeting to order at 6:32 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Dennis Robert Smith. Vice Chair John G. Mazza, and Commissioners
  Kraig Hill, Jeffrey D. Jennings, and Skylar Peak

  ALSO PRESENT: Monica Castillo, Assistant City Attorney; Todd Leishman, Assistant
  City Attorney; Richard Mollica, Planning Director; Tyler Eaton, Senior Planner; Joyce
  Parker-Bozylinski, Contract Planner: and Rebecca Evans, Recording Secretary

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Vice Chair Mazza moved and Commissioner Peak seconded a motion to approve
  the agenda as recommended by staffand to dedicate the meeting in memory ofJohn
  Wall.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recording Secretary Evans reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on March 9, 2023.

ITEM l  NEW PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A.  Local Coastal Program Amendment No. 18—002 and Zoning Text Amendment No.
  [8-004 — An amendment to the Local Coastal Program and Title 17 (Zoning) ofthe
  Malibu Municipal Code to update regulations related to Accessory Dwelling Units
  (Continued from March 6. 2023)
  Applicant:  City of Malibu
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of March 14‘ 2023
  Page 2 0f4

  Location:  Citywide
  Case Planners: Senior Planner Eaton and Contract Planner Parker-BozylinskL 456—
  2489” ext. 273
  Recommended Action: Adopt Planning Commission Resolution No. 23-12
  recommending that the City Council approve Local Coastal Program Amendment
  No. 18-002 and Zoning Text Amendment No. l8-004 for an amendment to the Local
  Coastal Program and to the Malibu Municipal Code to update regulations related to
  Accessory Dwelling Units.

  Contract Planner Parker-Bozylinski and Senior Planner Eaton presented the staff
  report.

  Chair Smith opened the public comment portion ofthe hearing.

  Speakers: Todd Spiegel, Jamie Francis, Howard Rudzki

  As there were no other speakers present, Chair Smith closed the public comment
  portion of the public hearing and returned the matter to the table for discussion.

MOTION  Chair Smith moved and Commissioner Jennings seconded a motion to adopt
  Planning Commission Resolution No. 23-12, as amended l) 2 / 12 pitch on roofs
  for single-family units; 2) recommending that the City Council approve Local
  Coastal Program Amendment No. 18-002 and Zoning Text Amendment No. l8—
  004 for an amendment to the Local Coastal Program and to the Malibu Municipal
  Code to update regulations related to Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs).

  The Commission discussed the motion and directed questions to staff.

  Todd Leishman presented the ADU statute and policy information to the
  Commission.

CONSENSUS The Commission reached consensus on a recommendation that ADUs should not
  be allowed to be used as short-term rental units.

CONSENSUSThe Commission reached consensus on a recommendation that ADUs would
  require a Site Plan Review for heights above 16 feet, with a maximum height of 24
  feet.

CONSENSUS Chair Smith called for a consensus vote on the recommended maximum size of
  ADUs as either 1.200 square feet or 900 square feet.

  By a 3-2 consensus vote. Commissioners Hill and Mazza dissenting. the
  Commission recommended a maximum size of 1.200 square feet for an ADU.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of March l4. 2023
  Page 3 0f4

CONSENSUS The COmmission reached c0nsensus 0n a recommendation that ADU basements,
  whether finished or unfinished. should be included in the total development square
  footage calculation in the Local Implementation Plan.

CONSENSUS The commission reached consensus on a recommendation that ADUs are to be
  between 400 square feet and 1,200 square feet.

CONSENSUS The Commission reached consensus to not recommend additional parking
  requirements for ADUs .

RECESS  Chair Smith recessed the meeting at 8:57 p.m. The meeting resumed at 9:05 p.m.
  with all Commissioners present.

SUBSTITUTE MOTION
  Chair Smith moved and Commissioner Jennings seconded the motion to adopt
  Planning Commission Resolution No. 23—12, as amended, l) set the parameters of
  ADUs to a height range of 16 ft. to 24 ft. pending site plan review and a square
  footage range of 400 sq. ft. to 1,200 sq. ft.; 2) parking requirements shall remain
  as-is, while removing the ability to install parking lifts; 3) owners shall be required
  to report rent amounts annually; 4) setback limitations shall remain the same as
  those listed in the Local Coastal Program Local Implementation Plan and the
  Malibu Muncipal Code; 5) basements attached to ADUs shall be included in the
  Total Development Square Footage; 6) staff shall ensure consistency ofthe listed
  height requirements for ADUs with the Malibu Municipal Code and the Local
  “Major  “Total
  Coastal Program; 7) revise term  Unit Size” to  Development Square
  Footage”; 8) multi-family unit ADUs shall be detached only; 9) require a 20-foot—
  minimum roadway width in order to build an ADU, regardless ofthe number of
  ingress or egress points; and lO) recommending that the City Council approve
  Local Coastal Program Amendment No. 18—002 and Zoning Text Amendment No.
  18-004 for an amendment to the Local Coastal Program and to the Malibu
  Municipal Code to update regulations related to Accessory Dwelling Units.

CONSENSUS Director Mollica requested consensus to direct Contract Planner Parker—Bozylinski
  to ensure that the final motion captured the amendments to Planning Commission
  Resolution No. 23-1 2 as determined by consensus throughout deliberations.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

CONSENSUSThe commission reached consensus to have a 20-foot-wide minimum roadway in
  order to build an Accessory Dwelling Unit. regardless of the number of ingress or
  egress pomts.
   Malibu Flaming Commission
  Minutes ofMarch I4. 2023
  Page 4 0f4

  The consensus carried 4-1, Chair Smith dissenting.

MOTION  Commissioner Jennings moved to adjourn the meeting. The motion failed for lack
  of a second.

MOTION  Vice Chair Mazza moved and Commissioner Jennings seconded the motion to have
  no requirement for a house to have two means of ingress or egress in order to build
  an Accessory Dwelling Unit.

  The question was called and the motion carried 3-2, Vice Chair Mazza and
  Commissioner Hill dissenting.

MOTION  Vice Chair Mazza moved and Commissioner Jennings seconded the motion to
  require a 20-foot-minimum width roadway in order to build an ADU, regardless of
  the number ofmeans of ingress 0r egress to the house.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION  At 10:44 p.m. Vice Chair Mazza moved and Commissioner Hill seconded a motion
  to adjourn the meeting in memory ofJohn Wall.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

  Approved and adopted by the Planning Commission of
  the City ofMalibu on May 5. 2025.
